_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28 for the 1904 target (T-1841), in the T-1840 sheet-census contract (tools/sheet_census.py). Every frontage row on the sheet and every named record on its ground is assigned here exactly once. Kinds and tiers as sheet-20.json. allocations[] gives service ground on this sheet to a named record placed on another sheet (the Pullman glasshouses) without moving that record; rulings[] settle the sheet's identity questions.

reading.by: Read by eye from the deposited sheet image (1642 x 2048 px), overview and full-resolution crops, 2026-10-09; the 1918 (1936) label at 6x.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, yellow frame, blue stone. A crossed square marks a stable. D = dwelling. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation. Garages are backcast as stables; uses, colours and unseen elevations remain for the build packages. The Calumet side of the sheet is counted by T-1946, not here. Footprints are not digitized and no dimension is claimed. The supplied 1911 sheet is the footprint layer for 1904 except where the expert guidance or a dated source says otherwise (docs/map-guidance.md); nothing on this sheet is named as changed between 1904 and 1911.

allocations.why: The two glasshouse ranges, the two-storey lodge between them and the open 18th Street ground east of the Kimball garage belong to the Pullman estate (pa-1729-5) and its package T-1934, not to the east-side service package T-1936. The basis is the placement of Beman's conservatory "across 18th Street from the house (toward Calumet)" in the image research, which this ground is; no deed has been read.

polygons.note_1904: The north-south "GREEN HO. GLASS RF." range east of the 20-foot alley behind 1811-1815. Assigned to the Pullman estate: the conservatory plates and photographs are placed in Pullman's private park across 18th Street from the house, toward Calumet, which is this ground; Pullman's house is on sheet 20. Glasshouses on the 1894 plate and still on the 1911 sheet, so standing in 1904.
The east-west "GREEN HO. GLASS ROOF" range with its rounded east end, joined to the north range. Same allocation as s28-pullman-greenhouse-north.
The two-storey brick dwelling ("D") at the angle of the two glasshouse ranges. Read as the estate's gardener's lodge; nothing names its occupant or use beyond the 1911 "D".
The unbuilt 18th Street ground east of the Kimball garage, bounded by the curve to Calumet: the "park" the conservatory stands in. No 1911 structure on it.

rulings.question: 1800-1900 identities
rulings.ruling: Every Prairie frontage on sheet 28 is joined to one named record, except 1828 (map-only, reconstructed) and 1908 (the second dwelling of the Edson Keith building). Every crosswalk row on this sheet moves from a candidate by printed number to a resolved join; the join rests on the printed number, the record's recorded lifespan and, where named, the image that shows the house.

rulings.question: 1900 versus 1906 photograph attribution
rulings.ruling: The sepia photograph posted by Glessner House as "1900 PA" and by Chicagology as "1906 Prairie" is one image of 1900 Prairie (Elbridge G. Keith): its mansard, hooded segmental windows, corner bay and Corinthian porch match the surviving 1900 facade, while 1906 was a brownstone front. The image is attributed to pa-1900-25 only; it is not evidence for the 1906 elevation.

rulings.question: Is 1908 a separate house?
rulings.ruling: No. The 1911 map draws 1906 and 1908 as one attached building; the Tribune (December 1918) lets "1904-1906 Prairie-av." as two residences of 28 rooms with one two-storey garage, and (1936) says number 1904 "adjoins the main building" and was the home of the son, Walter W. Keith; the 1904 Blue Book lists Walter W. Keith at 1904 and Mrs. Edson Keith at 1906. So the pair is one building of two dwellings, owned by pa-1906-34. The house numbers disagree (map 1906/1908, press and Blue Book 1904/1906) and are recorded, not reconciled.
rulings.replaceable_by: a permit or 1904 directory page giving the two halves' numbers

rulings.question: 1916/1930 versus Allerton 1936
rulings.ruling: Resolved on the map itself. The stacked label beside the southernmost west-side house reads "1918" over "(1936)", not "1916 (1930)"; the house drawn there, with its four-storey tower bay, is the Thompson/Allerton house, razed in 1915 (G23) and so still standing at the 1911 survey. The bare "1936" at the 20th Street corner is the frontage label of its open south grounds. One villa, on the drawn footprint; no second house at 1916 or 1930 and no vacant Allerton lot.

rulings.question: 1945 missing named record
rulings.ruling: Minted as pa-1945-armour-corwith: built for George Armour, designed by Treat & Foltz, completed 1872, long held by the Corwiths and razed in 1931 (G23, the Glessner House reading of the 1887 Ward Bros. view); the 1904 Blue Book lists Mrs. Henry Corwith and Charles R. Corwith at 1945.

rulings.question: Pullman service-garden allocation
rulings.ruling: The two glasshouse ranges, the two-storey lodge between them and the open 18th Street ground east of the Kimball garage belong to the Pullman estate (pa-1729-5) and its package T-1934, not to the east-side service package T-1936. The basis is the placement of Beman's conservatory "across 18th Street from the house (toward Calumet)" in the image research, which this ground is; no deed has been read.
rulings.replaceable_by: a deed or permit for the Calumet-side lots south of 18th Street
